content_units: Fast-Paced Fantasy Picks for a 13-Year-Old

These picks lean into   myth vibes, puzzles, quests, secrets, monsters, and strong momentum  . They avoid heavy, slow, description-first prose and are chosen to be easier entry points for a reader who wants a story to get moving quickly.
10 Books Likely to Hook a Reluctant Reader
Title & Author   Reading Level   Est. Pages   Why it may hook them

1     The Lock-Eater   by Zack Loran Clark   Middle grade to early YA   300–350   A thief, magical locks, secrets, and constant motion make this feel like a puzzle-box adventure instead of a slow fantasy novel.
2     The Gauntlet   by Karuna Riazi   Middle grade   250–320   Reads like being trapped inside a dangerous game, with riddles, teamwork, and fast chapter-to-chapter stakes.
3     Aru Shah and the End of Time   by Roshani Chokshi   Middle grade   300–360   Mythology-heavy but funny and quick, with Indian gods, cursed artifacts, and a strong “save the world now” pace.
4     The Serpent’s Secret   by Sayantani DasGupta   Middle grade   320–400   Packed with Bengali mythology, demons, shape-shifters, and cliffhangers that keep the plot moving.
5     The Storm Runner   by J.C. Cervantes   Middle grade   320–360   Maya mythology, monsters, and action start early; the voice is lively and very readable.
6     City of the Plague God   by Sarwat Chadda   Middle grade   350–450   Mesopotamian mythology plus modern danger gives it a big, cinematic feel without becoming hard to follow.

7     The False Prince   by Jennifer A. Nielsen   Middle grade to early YA   320–380   More political than mythic, but it’s built around schemes, deception, and a clever central mystery that rewards sharp readers.
8     The Book of Three   by Lloyd Alexander   Middle grade classic   150–230   Short, clean, and adventure-forward, with magical creatures and a quest structure that never gets too dense.
9     The Inquisitor’s Tale   by Adam Gidwitz   Middle grade   350–400   Medieval adventure with monsters, mystery, and a storyteller style that feels lively rather than textbook-serious.
10     Furthermore   by Tahereh Mafi   Middle grade   380–430   Color-based magic, weird challenges, and a quest through a surreal world give it strong wonder and puzzle energy.
Best Fits by Interest
If mythology is the top priority
-   Aru Shah and the End of Time
-   The Serpent’s Secret
-   The Storm Runner
-   City of the Plague God
If puzzles and clever twists matter most
-   The Lock-Eater
-   The Gauntlet
-   The False Prince
If fast pacing is the biggest need
-   The Gauntlet
-   The Storm Runner
-   Aru Shah and the End of Time
Strongest Starting Choices
Option 1:   Aru Shah and the End of Time     Funny, myth-filled, and quick to get going   Best all-around match

Good-to-Know Fit Notes
-   Easiest on dense prose:    The Book of Three ,  The Gauntlet ,  The Storm Runner
-   Most mythology-rich:    Aru Shah ,  The Serpent’s Secret ,  City of the Plague God
-   Most “just one more chapter”:    The False Prince ,  The Lock-Eater ,  The Gauntlet
- Page counts vary by edition, so ranges are more useful than exact numbers.
